choices.explanation: Incorrect: BCNF strengthens 3NF by requiring every nontrivial determinant to be a superkey; it is not the first stage described.

evidence.quote: 1NF requires atomic values in the chosen relational domains and no repeating groups in cells.
2NF requires 1NF and no nonprime attribute partially dependent on any candidate key.

For every nontrivial FD X→A, 3NF permits it when X is a superkey or A is prime. BCNF requires X to be a superkey. The mnemonic whole key and nothing but the key describes the common single-key case; it cannot replace the full tests when keys overlap. Remove dependencies of nonprime facts on nonkey determinants.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: Second normal form (2NF) Second normal form (2NF) is based on the concept of full functional dependency. A relation schema R is in 2NF if it is in 1NF and every non-prime attribute A in R is fully functionally dependent on the primary key (i.e. the non-prime attributes are not partially dependent on key attributes). Remove any partially dependent attributes and place them in another relation. A partial dependency is when the attribute(s) is/are dependent on a part of a key.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: Third Normal Form (3NF) A relation schema R is in third normal form (3NF) if it is in 2NF and every non-prime attribute of ‗R‘ are fully functionally dependent on every key of R and non-transitively dependent on every key of R.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of denormalization in database design for real-world scenarios?
questions.hint: Compare design techniques by the specific problem each solves.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 176

answer.explanation: Denormalization repeats or precomputes facts so that selected queries can perform less work, such as fewer joins. FDB38 also states the cost: more maintenance when underlying facts change. It does not aim to eliminate redundancy or enforce foreign-key references. A simpler query path may result, but a simpler schema is not the essential purpose.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Denormalization introduces controlled redundancy instead of eliminating it.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Its goal is to reduce costs of selected read queries using repeated or precomputed information.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Foreign-key constraints enforce references; denormalization itself does not establish referential integrity.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: It may simplify selected reads, but schema simplicity is not the defining or guaranteed goal.

evidence.quote: Normalization reduces dependency-driven anomalies. Indexing supplies search paths. Denormalization deliberately repeats or precomputes facts to reduce selected read costs, increasing maintenance work. Partitioning divides rows or columns; replication creates copies to improve locality or availability while complicating updates. These techniques can coexist. An e-commerce or gaming label alone does not select one.
Referential integrity requires a non-NULL foreign-key value to match an eligible referenced unique/candidate key; self-references are allowed.
Key integrity enforces uniqueness.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 4.4 Normalization Normalization is a process of organizing the data in database to avoid data redundancy, insertion anomaly, update anomaly & deletion anomaly. It is a technique of organizing the data in the database. It is a systematic approach of decomposing tables to eliminate data redundancy (repetition) and undesirable characteristics like Insertion, Update and Deletion Anomalies. It is a multi-step process that puts data into tabular form, removing duplicated data from the relation tables. Normal forms Redundancy in a relation may causes insertion, deletion, and update anomalies. Normalization is database design technique that minimizes redundancy from a relation or a set of relations. Normalization rules divides larger tables into smaller tables and links them using relationship.

questions.hint: Review inheritance, specialization and category constraints.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 178

answer.explanation: Object-oriented data modeling directly represents superclass/subclass inheritance. Enhanced ER also supports inheritance, but A is explicitly limited to basic ER in this question. Ordinary relational tables can encode subtype data through references without making inheritance a direct modeling construct, and document structure is not the object inheritance mechanism being tested. The scope distinction makes the selected technique definite.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Basic ER excludes the EER inheritance extension under the stated scope.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Object models directly support superclass/subclass inheritance.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Ordinary relational tables encode facts and references rather than directly declaring this inheritance construct.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Document structure is not the direct object inheritance model asked for.

evidence.quote: EER extends ER with superclass/subclass structure. A subclass inherits the superclass attributes and relationships. Specialization divides Student into Undergraduate and Graduate; generalization combines common properties into Student. Disjoint subclasses cannot overlap; overlapping subclasses can. Total specialization requires every superclass member in some subclass; partial specialization does not.
Object models also support inheritance; distinguish basic ER notation from EER when comparing models.
Structural EER inheritance alone does not define executable object methods.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: Types of Data Models 1. High-level or conceptual data models provide concepts that are close to the way many users perceive data. Entity – Relationship (E/R) model and Object-Oriented Model are examples of conceptual/high level data model.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 3.5 Enhanced Entity Relationship (EER) Model The complexityof the data is increasing so it becomes more and more difficult to use the traditional ER model for database modeling. To reduce this complexity of modeling we have to make improvements or enhancements to the existing ER model to make it able to handle the complex application in a better way. Enhanced ER (EER) model is a database model that incorporates the concepts of class/subclass relationships and type inheritance into the ER model. The EER model includes all the modeling

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: concepts of the ER model. In addition, it includes the concepts of subclass and superclass, categories (UNION types), attribute and relationship inheritance. EER is created to design more accurate database schemas. Subclasses and super classes can be thought as useful ways to describe similarities in the entities represented. Because subclasses inherit their attributes and relationships from the superclass, the database designer can represent complex, hierarchical interdependencies (inheritance) within the system being described.

questions.stem: Which CMS features directly support either semantic grouping of content or valid stored references between content and tags? Select all that apply.

answer.text: A. Referential integrity constraints; C. Content categorization and tagging
answer.explanation: Categories and tags describe semantic associations among content items. Referential integrity constraints keep the stored links between content and tags valid. These two features address meaning and reference validity respectively, so both fit. Full-text search supports finding text, while a distributed architecture concerns data placement and coordination. Neither is the requested direct representation or validation of content-to-tag relationships.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Referential constraints preserve valid links between content and related rows, such as tags.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Full-text search finds textual content rather than primarily defining or validating item relationships.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Categories and tags describe semantic groupings and associations among content items.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Distribution determines placement and coordination rather than directly representing the stated content relationships.

evidence.quote: In a CMS, tags/categories describe meaning, while foreign keys preserve valid references between content and tags. A ContentTag(ContentID,TagID) association models multiple tags per item; these functions complement each other.
Referential integrity requires a non-NULL foreign-key value to match an eligible referenced unique/candidate key; self-references are allowed.
Key integrity enforces uniqueness.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 3.3 ERD (Entity Relationship Diagram) ERD a graphical technique for representing a database schema. It is a modeling tool used to depict graphically a DB design before it is actually implemented. It shows the various entities being modeled and the important relationships among them. Referential Integrity ⚫ A ―foreign key‖ links each occurrence in a relation representing a child entity to the occurrence of the parent entity containing the matching candidate (usually primary) key ⚫ Referential Integrity means that if the foreign key contains a value, that value must refer to an existing occurrence in the parent entity

questions.stem:
Which database design technique is used to represent a hierarchical structure of data
elements?
questions.hint: Compare the data models by how they organize records and relationships.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 180

answer.explanation: A hierarchical structure organizes elements into parent-child levels. FDB02 assigns this representation to the hierarchical model, so C directly matches the requested design concept. Relational modeling instead uses tables, network modeling permits more general record links, and richer object-relational types do not by themselves require a hierarchical organization.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Relational modeling represents facts in tables rather than requiring a hierarchical tree.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Network modeling permits linked records with multiple parents rather than a restricted hierarchy.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Hierarchical modeling explicitly represents the parent-child structure asked for in the stem.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: An object-relational approach adds richer types to relational storage rather than defining this tree organization.

evidence.quote: A data model supplies concepts for structure, relationships, constraints and operations. Conceptual ER models describe entities and relationships. Relational models use tables; hierarchical models organize records in a parent–child tree; classic network models connect records through pointer-based owner/member links, allowing multiple parents. Object models represent objects with identity, state and behavior. A physical model specifies record layouts and access paths. These are different representation choices, not stages of one query.
Richer relational types do not by themselves require all data to form a parent–child tree; that representation is the defining concern of hierarchical modeling.
An object-relational DBMS retains relational data management while supporting richer extensions such as user-defined data types, functions and operators.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: Types of Data Models 1. High-level or conceptual data models provide concepts that are close to the way many users perceive data. Entity – Relationship (E/R) model and Object-Oriented Model are examples of conceptual/high level data model. 2. Low-level or physical data models provide concepts that describe the details of how data is stored on the computer storage media. Concepts provided by physical data models are generally meant for computer specialists, not for end users. 3. representational (or implementation) data model provides concepts that may be easily understood by end users but that are not too far from the way data is organized in computer storage. Representational data models hide many details of data storage on disk but can be implemented on a computer system directly. The widely used relational data models are the network and hierarchical.

questions.stem: Which benefit directly follows from reducing dependency-driven insertion, deletion and update anomalies through normalization, without assuming reduced storage or simpler queries?
questions.hint: Distinguish dependency-based design problems from the contents of one sample table.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 181

answer.explanation: Normalization separates facts according to their determinants, reducing repeated facts and the insertion, deletion and update anomalies they cause. That directly supports enhanced data integrity. Storage savings and simpler retrieval are not guaranteed because decomposition can introduce additional keys and joins. Increased redundancy is opposite to the intended reduction of avoidable repetition, so it is not the benefit identified by this question.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Normalized retrieval may require more joins, so simplification does not follow.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Normalization aims to reduce avoidable repetition.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Reducing inconsistent updates and related anomalies improves integrity.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Storage savings can be offset by extra keys and relation overhead.

evidence.quote: Suppose Enrollment repeats StudentName for every course. An update anomaly requires changing every copy of the student's name; missed copies disagree. An insertion anomaly prevents recording a new student until some enrollment exists. A deletion anomaly loses the only record of a student's details when their last enrollment is deleted. Revoke anomaly is not a normalization anomaly.
Normalization separates facts according to their determinants, reducing avoidable repetition and associated anomalies.
Reduced redundancy can improve integrity and storage use, but extra keys and joins mean neither storage savings nor faster retrieval is guaranteed.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 4.3 Database Anomalies Database Anomalies are the flaws in databases which occurs because of poor database design and storing everything in a single flat database. They are problems that are caused usually by redundant data. Types of database anomalies are Insertion anomaly, Deletion anomaly, and Update anomaly. Insertion Anomaly - occurs when the entire primary key is not known and the database cannot insert a new record properly. This would violate entity integrity. It can be avoided by using a sequence number for the primary key. Deletion Anomaly - happens when a record is deleted that results in the loss of other related data. It can be avoided by normalizing tables in a database to minimize their dependency. Update Anomaly - occurs when a change to one attribute value causes the database to either contain inconsistent data or causes multiple records to need changing. It may be prevented by making sure tables are in third normal form. 4.4 Normalization Normalization is a process of organizing the data in database to avoid data redundancy, insertion anomaly, update anomaly & deletion anomaly. It is a technique of organizing the data in the database. It is a systematic approach of decomposing tables to eliminate data redundancy (repetition) and undesirable characteristics like Insertion, Update and Deletion Anomalies. It is a multi-step process that puts data into tabular form, removing duplicated data from the relation tables. Normal forms Redundancy in a relation may causes insertion, deletion, and update anomalies. Normalization is database design technique that minimizes redundancy from a relation or a set of relations. Normalization rules divides larger tables into smaller tables and links them using relationship. Normal Forms are maintenance rules that are used to eliminate or reduce the redundancy in database relations. These normal forms are 1NF (First Normal Form), 2NF (Second Normal Form)

questions.stem:
Which database design concept allows the division of a large database into smaller,
manageable units?
questions.hint: Distinguish logical records, disk pages and physical file organization.
sources: Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 182

answer.explanation: FDB24 explicitly contrasts partitioning, replication, migration and archiving. Partitioning divides the dataset into smaller portions, matching the question. Replication makes additional copies, migration moves data, and archiving takes older data out of active service. Those operations can accompany partitioning, but none of them defines division into manageable units.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Partitioning divides a large dataset into smaller portions or manageable units.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Replication creates copies rather than dividing the original dataset into distinct units.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Migration moves data to another location or system rather than defining a split.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Archiving removes older data from active service rather than generally dividing the database.

evidence.quote: A page/block is a unit of database I/O and holds several records. For fixed unspanned records of size r in usable page space B, the blocking factor is floor(B/r), and n records occupy ceil(n/blocking factor) pages. Page headers and slots reduce usable space.
Partitioning splits a large dataset; replication copies it; migration moves it; archiving removes older data from active service.
A heap has no search-key order and supports simple inserts, but searches may scan all pages.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 6.2 Data Replication and Fragmentation: Distributed data storage  There are two approaches to store the relation in the distributed database : Replication and Fragmentation I. Data Replication  The system maintain several identical copies of the relation & store each copy at a different site  In general it enhance the performance of read operation and increase the availability of data to read only transaction. However, update transactions incur greater overhead II. Data Fragmentation – Split a relation into logically related and correct parts. – The main reasons for fragmenting a relation are • Efficiency- data that is not needed by the local applications is not stored • Parallelism – a transaction can be divided into several subqueries that operate on fragments which will increase the degree of concurrency – but reconstruction of the whole relation will require accessing data from all sites

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: • A relation can be fragmented in two ways:  Horizontal fragmentation • It is a horizontal subset of a relation which contain those of rows which satisfy selection conditions. • Consider the Employee relation with selection condition (DNO = 5). All rows satisfy this condition will create a subset which will be a horizontal fragment of Employee relation. • A selection condition may be composed of several conditions connected by AND or OR.  Vertical fragmentation • It is a subset of a relation which is created by a subset of columns. Thus a vertical fragment of a relation will contain values of selected columns. – Consider the Employee relation. A vertical fragment of can be created by keeping the values of Name, Bdate, Sex, and Address. – Because there is no condition for creating a vertical fragment, each fragment must include the primary key attribute of the parent relation Employee. In this way all vertical fragments of a relation are connected.

Which database design technique is used to capture the relationships between entities in a
graphical representation?

answer.explanation: ERD is explicitly a graphical database-schema technique showing modeled entities and their important relationships. This directly establishes ER modeling for the graphical representation asked about.

An entity type describes common properties; its current collection of entities is an entity set. A relationship associates entities. In Chen notation rectangles represent entity types, diamonds relationships and ellipses attributes; double ellipses denote multivalued attributes and dashed ellipses derived attributes. Always inspect the diagram legend.
Conceptual ER models describe entities and relationships.
Relational models use tables; hierarchical models organize records in a parent–child tree; classic network models connect records through pointer-based owner/member links, allowing multiple parents.

module_refs.quote: 3.3 ERD (Entity Relationship Diagram) ERD a graphical technique for representing a database schema. questions.stem: In contrary to the traditional file-based approach, in the database approach:

options.label: A
options.text: Programs define and access their own data

options.label: B
options.text: Store data items in multiple copies

options.label: C
options.text: Don't care about the definition of programs and data

options.label: D
options.text: Data and programs are defined independently

questions.hint: Trace which schema levels a proposed change affects.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 49

answer.text: Data and programs are defined independently
answer.explanation: The database approach insulates programs from data definitions and supports data independence. This is the relevant distinction from programs managing their own files.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Own program-specific definitions do not express the database approach's insulation. (PDF pp. 5, 6, 8.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Multiple uncontrolled copies are not the defining benefit and can cause inconsistency. (PDF pp. 5, 6, 8.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The approach explicitly maintains metadata and definitions, not indifference to them. (PDF pp. 5, 6, 8.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Independent definitions match program/data insulation and independence. (PDF pp. 5, 6, 8.)

evidence.quote: Physical data independence permits changing internal storage without changing the conceptual schema, for example adding an index. Logical data independence permits conceptual changes while preserving affected external views and application interfaces, for example splitting a table while maintaining a compatible view. It is harder because applications depend on logical meaning. Data abstraction hides irrelevant details; program–data insulation separates data definitions from application code.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 1.2 Database System versus File System The traditional file processing system is file-directory structure supported by a conventional operating system. A file system organization of data lucks a number of major features of a database system, such as Data redundancy and inconsistency, Difficulty in accessing data, Data isolation, Integrity problems, Atomicity problems, Concurrent access anomalies. 1.3 Characteristics of the Database Approach The main characteristics of the database approach are Self-describing nature, Data abstraction and Insulation between programs and data, Support of multiple views of the data, sharing of data and multiuser transaction processing.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: Data abstraction and Insulation between programs and data- Data Abstraction is a process of hiding unwanted or irrelevant details from the end user. It provides a different view and helps in achieving data independence which is used to enhance the security of data.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 2.4 Data Independence The three-schema architecture can be used to further explain the concept of data independence, which can be defined as the capacity to change the schema at one level of a database system without having to change the schema at the next higher level. The two types of data independence: 1. Logical data independence is the capacity to change the conceptual schema without having to change external schemas or application programs. 2. Physical data independence is the capacity to change the internal schema without having to change the conceptual schema. Hence, the external schemas do not need be changed as well.

questions.stem:
Assume you are a database designer and you are given a task to specify entities, relationships,
constraints on relations and data types for the data to be stored. At which level of the three-schema architecture
would this be addressed?
questions.hint: Trace which schema levels a proposed change affects.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 50

answer.explanation: The conceptual level describes the whole database and explicitly concentrates on entities, data types, relationships, operations and constraints while hiding physical storage. The stem repeats those conceptual responsibilities.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: View level shows a user-group subset. (PDF pp. 7, 8.)

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Internal level describes physical storage and access paths. (PDF pp. 7, 8.)

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: External is another name for user view, not the global description. (PDF pp. 7, 8.)

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Conceptual is the level explicitly listing the requested structural components. (PDF pp. 7, 8.)

evidence.quote: The external level gives each user group a selected view. The conceptual level describes the whole logical database: entity types, relationships, data types and constraints. The internal/physical level describes files, record placement and access paths. These are abstraction levels, distinct from client/server deployment tiers.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 2.3 Three-schema Architecture and Data Independence The goal of the three-schema architecture is to separate the user applications from the physical database. In this architecture, schemas can be defined at the following three levels: 1. The internal level has an internal schema, which describes the physical storage structure of the database. The internal schema uses a physical data model and describes the complete details of data storage and access paths for the database.

module_refs.title: Fundamental of Database Systems module
module_refs.quote: 2. The conceptual level has a conceptual schema, which describes the structure of the whole database for users. The conceptual schema hides the details of physical storage structures and concentrates on describing entities, data types, relationships, user operations, and constraints. 3. The external or view level includes a number of external schemas or user views. Each external schema describes the part of the database that a particular user group is interested in and hides the rest of the database from that user group.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of normalization in database design?

options.label: A
options.text: To reduce redundancy and improve data integrity

options.label: C
options.text: To create complex relationships between tables

questions.hint: Distinguish dependency-based design problems from the contents of one sample table.
sources: Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 53

answer.text: Reduce avoidable redundancy and associated integrity anomalies.
answer.explanation: FDB19 defines normalization as separating facts according to their determinants, reducing avoidable repetition and insertion, deletion and update anomalies. That supports both parts of A. It does not promise universally faster queries, deliberately create complexity for its own sake or encrypt content. Performance and security need their own workload and threat-model choices.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Normalization reduces repeated facts and the anomalies that threaten data consistency.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: More joins may be needed, so faster query execution is not a universal normalization purpose.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Relationships follow fact dependencies; creating complexity is not the goal.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Normalization restructures facts and does not encrypt sensitive values.

evidence.quote: Suppose Enrollment repeats StudentName for every course. An update anomaly requires changing every copy of the student's name; missed copies disagree. An insertion anomaly prevents recording a new student until some enrollment exists. A deletion anomaly loses the only record of a student's details when their last enrollment is deleted. Revoke anomaly is not a normalization anomaly.
Normalization separates facts according to their determinants, reducing avoidable repetition and associated anomalies.
Adding a generated row ID may make insertion technically possible, but does not remove repeated facts or fix the dependency design.

questions.stem: A weak entity uses its partial key together with the key of an independently keyed owner. Which terms describe that associated entity set? Select all that apply.
questions.hint: Check how a dependent entity obtains its complete identity.

answer.text: B. Strong entity set; D. Owner set
answer.explanation: The weak entity lacks a complete independent identifier. Its owner's key combines with the partial key to identify it. Because the owner is independently keyed in this question, strong entity set and owner set both describe the associated set. Identifying describes the relationship connecting the sets, while neighbor does not state the necessary ownership and identification dependency.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Identifying is normally the relationship role rather than the defined name of the owner entity set.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: The owner that supplies an independent identifying key is normally a strong entity set.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Neighbor does not express the necessary ownership and identification dependency.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Owner set is the associated entity set whose key identifies the weak entity together with its partial key.

evidence.quote: A weak entity lacks a complete independent key. Its owner is normally a strong entity, so owner entity set and strong entity set may both describe the associated set. Its partial key, also called discriminator, distinguishes weak entities of the same owner. Identification combines the owner key and partial key.
The weak entity participates totally in its identifying relationship.
Chen notation uses a double rectangle, double identifying diamond and dashed underline for a partial key.

questions.stem:
A language that allows the DBA or user to describe and name the entities, attributes, and 
relationships required for the application is__________
questions.hint: Classify each SQL command by the kind of change it performs.

answer.explanation: Describing and naming application entities, attributes and relationships defines schema structure. FDB26 assigns structural changes to DDL through CREATE, ALTER and DROP. TCL manages transaction boundaries, DCL controls privileges and DML retrieves or changes data. These categories have different effects, so DDL uniquely matches the schema-description role in the stem.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: TCL manages commit, rollback and savepoints rather than defining schema elements.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: DCL manages privileges through GRANT and REVOKE rather than describing entities and attributes.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: DML retrieves or changes instance data rather than defining the application schema.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: DDL defines and changes schema structure, including tables, attributes and constraints.

evidence.quote: DDL changes structure: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, commonly RENAME and TRUNCATE in textbook classifications. DML retrieves or changes data: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE. Some texts separate SELECT as DQL. DCL manages privileges through GRANT and REVOKE. TCL includes COMMIT, ROLLBACK and SAVEPOINT. Classify a statement by its effect, not its length.

questions.stem: In relational-table terminology, which terms describe a unit of related field values treated together by an application? Select all that apply.
questions.hint: Distinguish a relation's structure from its current contents and its descriptive metadata.

answer.explanation: A tuple holds a set of related attribute values as one table unit. Row and record are synonymous names for that unit, so both alternatives qualify. A field is only an individual property, and a database is the larger coherent collection of related data. Grammatical number in Rows does not create a different relational concept from Record.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Rows contain related field values and are the relational counterpart of records.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: A field is an individual property rather than a collection of related fields.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Record is the stated unit that groups related fields for application use.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: A database contains a larger coherent collection of data rather than just one record.

evidence.quote: A relation is a set of tuples, represented as a table. A tuple/row/record contains related attribute values; an attribute/column/field describes a property. Degree counts columns; cardinality counts rows. Classical relations have distinct tuples, atomic cells and domains for attributes; row order has no meaning. Column order has no logical meaning when attributes are identified by name. SQL tables can contain duplicate rows unless constrained.

questions.stem: Which template creates a table with one column? Treat table_name, column_name and column_type as placeholders for valid identifiers and a data type.
questions.hint: Distinguish table definition changes from changes to stored rows.

answer.explanation: CREATE TABLE introduces a new table definition. Within its parentheses, each column declaration places the column name before its data type, without a comma between those two parts. Commas separate whole declarations. Option C matches this pattern. A and B omit TABLE, while D reverses and separates the intended name/type pair and therefore fails the requested template.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: TABLE is absent and the column declaration is split incorrectly.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: TABLE is absent and the name/type order is reversed.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: The name/type pair forms one complete column declaration.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The type/name order and comma do not form the intended declaration.

evidence.quote: CREATE TABLE Employee (EmpID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR(80)); declares two columns. The name and its type stay together; the comma separates whole column declarations. To add a primary key later: ALTER TABLE Employee ADD PRIMARY KEY (EmpID); existing data must be unique and non-NULL. A table cannot gain a second primary key without replacing the existing constraint.

questions.stem: From the following alternatives which one is FALSE about database system?

options.label: A
options.text: It is very difficult to protect a file under the system

options.label: B
options.text: In database system the user is not required to write the procedures

options.label: C
options.text: In database system, DBMS provides a good protection mechanism.

options.label: D
options.text: It contains a wide variety of sophisticated techniques to store and retrieve the data.

questions.hint: Review the database approach and match each claimed benefit or cost to its mechanism.

answer.text: The claim that protection is very difficult under a database system is false.
answer.explanation: FDB01 contrasts unmanaged file difficulties with DBMS authorization, shared integrity, transactions and recovery. A therefore reverses a stated database benefit. B is understood in the data-access sense: declarative requests need not prescribe retrieval procedures, as FDB36 explains; it does not mean applications never contain code. Protection and sophisticated storage/access facilities in C and D are consistent with the note.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: This reverses the note's benefit: a DBMS provides coordinated protection rather than inherently making protection very difficult.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Declarative data requests need not prescribe retrieval procedures; this does not exclude ordinary application code.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Authorization and controlled data access are explicit DBMS protection mechanisms.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: DBMS storage and access facilities include indexes, buffers, query processing and other sophisticated mechanisms.

evidence.quote: A database is a coherent collection of related facts with meaning for an application. A DBMS is software that defines, stores, retrieves, updates, protects and shares that data. The database is the content; the DBMS manages it. A database system also includes applications, people and infrastructure.
Traditional file applications define their own formats and access procedures.
A DBMS centralizes metadata and supports multiple views, authorization, transactions, backup and recovery.

questions.stem:
Consider a directed line(->) from the relationship set advisor to both entity sets instructor 
and student. This indicates _________ cardinality
questions.hint: Read the relationship in both directions and check participation constraints.

answer.text: One-to-one under the common ER arrow convention.
answer.explanation: FDB09 explicitly discusses arrows from advisor to both Instructor and Student. Under its common convention, each arrow imposes a maximum of one on the corresponding end. Both ends are therefore maximum-one, producing 1:1. This does not imply total participation, and another diagram notation would require a legend, but the complete note supplies the convention for this example.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Many-to-one permits many at one end, contrary to maximum-one arrows at both ends.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Many-to-many imposes neither of the maximum-one constraints stated by the arrows.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Maximum one at both ends produces a one-to-one relationship.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: One-to-many permits multiple associations at one end rather than maximum one at both.

evidence.quote: Read business rules in both directions. If each employee belongs to one department and each department has many employees, Employee→Department is N:1; Department→Employee is 1:N. Building→Location could also be N:1, so names alone cannot select a unique example. Under the common arrow convention, arrows from advisor to both Instructor and Student impose maximum-one at both ends, giving 1:1. Without a notation convention, arrows are unsafe evidence.

questions.stem: What is the basic goal of Normalization?
questions.hint: Distinguish dependency-based design problems from the contents of one sample table.

answer.explanation: Normalization separates facts by their determinants to reduce repeated storage and the anomalies that repetition can cause. FDB19 therefore supports reducing redundancy as the basic listed goal. Decreasing integrity is the opposite intended effect, and maximizing transitive or unspecified dependencies is not a normalization objective. Proper dependencies are analyzed rather than increased indiscriminately.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Normalization aims to improve integrity by reducing anomalies, not decrease it.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Reducing avoidable repeated facts is a basic normalization goal.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Problematic nonkey transitive dependencies are removed or separated rather than maximized.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Dependencies are analyzed to place facts correctly; increasing them indiscriminately is not the objective.

evidence.quote: Suppose Enrollment repeats StudentName for every course. An update anomaly requires changing every copy of the student's name; missed copies disagree. An insertion anomaly prevents recording a new student until some enrollment exists. A deletion anomaly loses the only record of a student's details when their last enrollment is deleted. Revoke anomaly is not a normalization anomaly.
Normalization separates facts according to their determinants, reducing avoidable repetition and associated anomalies.
Remove dependencies of nonprime facts on nonkey determinants.

questions.stem: For a relation with ID, CITY and NAME, ID is guaranteed unique and non-NULL while CITY and NAME may repeat. Which listed sets are superkeys? Select all that apply.
questions.hint: Test uniqueness and minimality separately when classifying keys.

answer.explanation: A superkey is any set of attributes guaranteed to identify a tuple. ID has that guarantee, and the larger set containing CITY and ID keeps it. Both sets therefore qualify, even though the larger one is not minimal. CITY and NAME may repeat and cannot independently identify all tuples. Minimality would distinguish candidate keys, but it is not required for superkeys.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: Repeated names are permitted, so NAME is not guaranteed unique.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: ID uniquely identifies every tuple.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: Repeated cities are permitted, so CITY is not guaranteed unique.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: Including unique ID preserves identification even with the extra CITY attribute.

evidence.quote: A superkey uniquely identifies a tuple. A candidate key is a minimal superkey: removing any component loses uniqueness. Minimal means no unnecessary attribute, not necessarily the fewest columns among all keys. A primary key is one selected candidate key; remaining candidates are alternate keys. A composite key contains multiple attributes and need not be the chosen primary key.
If ID is unique, both {ID} and {ID,City} are superkeys, but only {ID} is minimal.
A table can have several candidates and foreign keys but at most one declared primary-key constraint, possibly containing several columns.

questions.stem:
______________is one of the candidate keys chosen by the database designer to uniquely 
identify the entity set.
questions.hint: Test uniqueness and minimality separately when classifying keys.

answer.explanation: FDB07 defines a primary key as the selected candidate key, with the remaining candidates called alternate keys. The stem asks specifically for the designer's selection rather than every unique attribute set. Superkey is broader and candidate key denotes eligibility before selection. A social-security identifier could be chosen, but is not the generic name of that role.

choices.label: A
choices.explanation: A superkey is any unique identifier set and may include unnecessary attributes.

choices.label: B
choices.explanation: Candidate keys are eligible minimal identifiers, not specifically the one selected for the primary role.

choices.label: C
choices.explanation: A social-security identifier is a possible attribute choice, not the generic selected-key category.

choices.label: D
choices.explanation: The selected candidate key is the primary key.

questions.stem: What is the difference between a primary key and a foreign key?
questions.hint: Test uniqueness and minimality separately when classifying keys.

answer.text: A primary key is the selected unique non-NULL identifier; a foreign key references an eligible key.
answer.explanation: FDB07 defines the primary key as a selected candidate key. FDB15 requires non-NULL foreign-key values to match an eligible referenced unique/candidate key; foreign keys need not be unique and may permit NULL.

evidence.quote: A superkey uniquely identifies a tuple. A candidate key is a minimal superkey: removing any component loses uniqueness. Minimal means no unnecessary attribute, not necessarily the fewest columns among all keys. A primary key is one selected candidate key; remaining candidates are alternate keys. Entity integrity requires every primary-key component to be non-NULL.

questions.stem: Why is database normalization important? What problems does it solve?
questions.hint: Distinguish dependency-based design problems from the contents of one sample table.

answer.text: Normalization reduces repeated facts and insertion, deletion and update anomalies.
answer.explanation: Repeating a student name across enrollments risks inconsistent updates, prevents storing some facts without unrelated rows and can lose a fact when its last repeated row is deleted. Normalization separates facts by their determinants to reduce these anomalies.

evidence.quote: Suppose Enrollment repeats StudentName for every course. An update anomaly requires changing every copy of the student's name; missed copies disagree. An insertion anomaly prevents recording a new student until some enrollment exists. A deletion anomaly loses the only record of a student's details when their last enrollment is deleted. Revoke anomaly is not a normalization anomaly.
Normalization separates facts according to their determinants, reducing avoidable repetition and associated anomalies.
Adding a generated row ID may make insertion technically possible, but does not remove repeated facts or fix the dependency design.

questions.stem: What happens if you UPDATE a row but forget to include a WHERE clause?
questions.hint: Track which rows each data-changing command affects.

answer.text: UPDATE without WHERE targets every row, subject to constraints and transaction outcome.
answer.explanation: FDB29 states that an UPDATE without WHERE targets every row. The SET expressions are therefore applied to all rows rather than one intended row; constraints or errors can still prevent completion.

evidence.quote: INSERT INTO Hotel(HotelID,HotelName,SubCity) VALUES (1,'Hilton','Yeka'); pairs each named column with a compatible value. Counts and types must match; keys and other constraints still apply. Without a column list, values must follow the table's declared column order.
UPDATE without WHERE targets every row.
UPDATE Book SET Price = 600 WHERE ID = 'B001'; changes matching rows.

questions.stem: Why would you use a ROLLBACK command in a transaction?
questions.hint: Match each transaction guarantee to its precise failure or interference scenario.

answer.text: ROLLBACK undoes uncommitted transaction work, for example after a failure or unwanted change.
answer.explanation: FDB37 contrasts COMMIT, which completes transaction work, with ROLLBACK, which undoes uncommitted work. Rollback restores the prior transactional state after errors or a decision not to keep the changes; it does not erase other users' committed transactions.

evidence.quote: For a transfer, subtracting 100 from one balance and adding 100 to another must commit together; losing either half violates atomicity and may violate the total-balance invariant. BEGIN starts work, COMMIT completes it, ROLLBACK undoes uncommitted work and SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate rollback point. A failed transaction may roll back while other users' committed transactions remain. SQL transaction syntax and error-handling constructs differ by DBMS; @@ERROR/IF is SQL Server-specific.

questions.stem: What is the difference between DELETE and DROP?
questions.hint: Classify each SQL command by the kind of change it performs.

answer.text: DELETE removes rows and retains the table; DROP TABLE removes the table object.
answer.explanation: FDB26 distinguishes data deletion from structural removal. DELETE may target selected rows with WHERE, or all rows without it, while leaving the table defined. DROP TABLE removes that relation object.

evidence.quote: DELETE removes rows and keeps the table; DROP TABLE removes the table object; ALTER changes its definition. TRUNCATE empties a table using implementation-specific mechanisms. PostgreSQL allows transactional rollback of TRUNCATE, so no rollback information is retained is not a universal SQL property. SQL Server permits DROP DATABASE Sales, suppliers; that comma-list syntax is vendor-specific. SQLite's .databases lists attached names/files in its command-line shell; .database is not the documented command.
UPDATE without WHERE targets every row.
DELETE FROM r; removes every row but leaves r defined.

notes.title: Records, pages and primary file organization

blocks.text: A page/block is a unit of database I/O and holds several records.
For fixed unspanned records of size r in usable page space B, the blocking factor is floor(B/r), and n records occupy ceil(n/blocking factor) pages.
Page headers and slots reduce usable space.
A heap has no search-key order and supports simple inserts, but searches may scan all pages.
A sorted file supports efficient range scans and binary search on the ordering field, with more costly insertions or overflow handling.
A hashed file chooses a bucket by hash(key), supports equality lookup well and requires collision/overflow handling; hash order does not support ordinary ranges.
Choose organization from actual reads, writes and predicates.
Partitioning splits a large dataset; replication copies it; migration moves it; archiving removes older data from active service.

Advanced Database Systems module

notes.title: Ordered, dense, sparse and multilevel indexes

blocks.text: An index stores search keys with pointers or row identifiers.
It often speeds selective retrieval but consumes space and must be maintained on writes.
A full scan can win for a tiny table or a query returning most rows.
Indexes do not themselves establish referential integrity.
In ordered-file indexing terminology, a primary ordered index is on the file’s ordering key and can have one entry per page, hence sparse.
A clustering index is on a nonunique ordering field, often with an entry per distinct value.
Secondary indexes provide other access paths and must represent all searchable values with record pointers or pointer lists.
A dense index represents each search value; sparse indexes rely on ordered data between entries.
Multilevel indexes index lower index levels.
B/B+ trees support ordered and range search; hashing targets equality; bitmap indexes suit some analytic workloads.
No one type is universally best.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module

notes.title: SQL command categories and exact scope

blocks.text: DDL changes structure: CREATE, ALTER, DROP, commonly RENAME and TRUNCATE in textbook classifications.
DML retrieves or changes data: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
Some texts separate SELECT as DQL.
DCL manages privileges through GRANT and REVOKE.
TCL includes COMMIT, ROLLBACK and SAVEPOINT.
Classify a statement by its effect, not its length.
DELETE removes rows and keeps the table; DROP TABLE removes the table object; ALTER changes its definition.
TRUNCATE empties a table using implementation-specific mechanisms.
PostgreSQL allows transactional rollback of TRUNCATE, so no rollback information is retained is not a universal SQL property.
SQL Server permits DROP DATABASE Sales, suppliers; that comma-list syntax is vendor-specific.
SQLite's .databases lists attached names/files in its command-line shell; .database is not the documented command.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
PostgreSQL: TRUNCATE
Microsoft: DROP DATABASE (Transact-SQL)
SQLite: Command-line shell
SELECT Name,Address FROM Customer; produces only those mailing-label fields.
SELECT * selects all columns; DISTINCT removes duplicate result rows; AS supplies an alias; ALL permits duplicates and does not mean all columns.
SQL normally preserves duplicates without DISTINCT.
A query reading table columns needs an appropriate FROM source.
A literal-only query such as SELECT 1 may legally omit FROM.
Typical written clause order is SELECT … FROM … WHERE … GROUP BY … HAVING … ORDER BY ….
Conceptually form FROM/JOIN rows, filter WHERE, group, filter HAVING, select expressions and then order the result.
SELECT alone normally reads without changing the database state.
WHERE alone is a clause rather than a complete read-only statement, so it cannot be compared as an equivalent executable command.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
Use single quotes for SQL string literals: WHERE ID = 'B001'.
Standard double quotes delimit identifiers, although some vendor modes accept them for strings.
Qualify ambiguous columns with aliases such as E.Department.
Conditions use =, <>, <, >, AND, OR and NOT; use parentheses to make precedence clear.
LIKE 'Ab%' matches a prefix, and BETWEEN includes its endpoints.
NULL represents a missing/unknown value.
Comparisons such as Salary = NULL are unknown, not true; use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL.
WHERE retains only true conditions.
An index-friendly year predicate for timestamps is BirthDate >= DATE '2000-01-01' AND BirthDate < DATE '2001-01-01', avoiding omitted times on December 31.
Expression indexes can support functions, so functions do not universally prevent indexing.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
INSERT INTO Hotel(HotelID,HotelName,SubCity) VALUES (1,'Hilton','Yeka'); pairs each named column with a compatible value.
Counts and types must match; keys and other constraints still apply.
Without a column list, values must follow the table's declared column order.
UPDATE Book SET Price = 600 WHERE ID = 'B001'; changes matching rows.
UPDATE without WHERE targets every row.
DELETE FROM Publisher WHERE Name = 'XWZ'; deletes matching publisher rows, subject to reference policies.
DELETE FROM r; removes every row but leaves r defined.
Both clear relation entries and delete rows describe that effect.
Several UPDATE statements can all be valid while performing different tasks; most appropriate requires a requested change and a specified quoting dialect.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
CREATE TABLE Employee (EmpID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR(80)); declares two columns.
The name and its type stay together; the comma separates whole column declarations.
To add a primary key later: ALTER TABLE Employee ADD PRIMARY KEY (EmpID); existing data must be unique and non-NULL.
A table cannot gain a second primary key without replacing the existing constraint.
ALTER TABLE Employee ADD COLUMN Email VARCHAR(120); adds a column in PostgreSQL-style syntax.
ALTER TABLE Employee DROP COLUMN Email; removes it.
ALTER TABLE Employee ADD CONSTRAINT uq_email UNIQUE (Email); adds a named constraint.
Use ALTER rather than DALTER, and do not separate column_name and column_type with a comma; validate the resulting SQL before execution.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
An inner join returns matching pairs satisfying ON.
An equijoin uses equality; a theta join permits another comparison.
A natural join is ordinarily an inner equality join on every same-named column and merges those duplicate columns.
JOIN … USING (DeptID) specifies shared join columns explicitly.
CROSS JOIN forms every pair without a matching condition.
LEFT OUTER JOIN also preserves unmatched left rows, padding right columns with NULL; RIGHT preserves right rows and FULL preserves both.
Therefore inner and natural inner joins both discard unmatched rows.
A self-join uses aliases for two occurrences of one base table.
Each ordinary join operator combines two inputs, but its inputs can be earlier joins, so one query can join many tables.
Distinguish base-table count, table occurrences and binary operator arity.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
PostgreSQL: Table expressions
COUNT(*) counts rows, COUNT(x) counts non-NULL x values; SUM and AVG summarize non-NULL numeric values.
SQL's usual average function is AVG, not AVERAGE.
GROUP BY creates one group per distinct grouping value; HAVING tests aggregate groups after WHERE has filtered individual rows.
SELECT Department, AVG(Salary) FROM Employee WHERE Department <> 'Sales' GROUP BY Department HAVING AVG(Salary) > 35000; lists qualifying department averages.
An ordinary AVG(Salary) predicate cannot be placed directly in WHERE.
Selecting EmpID, FirstName and LastName while grouping only by Department is also invalid unless the DBMS can establish the required functional dependence.
The grouping column need not itself appear in SELECT; check the functional dependence of other selected columns.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
PostgreSQL: GROUP BY and HAVING
A subquery is a SELECT nested inside another statement.
It may appear in WHERE, HAVING or FROM, not only the first two.
IN tests membership; EXISTS tests whether at least one qualifying row exists.
Correlated subqueries refer to the outer row.
A scalar subquery must produce an appropriate single value.
Beware NOT IN when its subquery can return NULL; NOT EXISTS often expresses the intended absence more safely.
CREATE VIEW CSStudent AS SELECT StudentID,Name FROM Student WHERE Major = 'CS'; stores a query definition and presents a virtual table.
Views can simplify repeated queries, expose derived values and restrict access when configured correctly.
An ordinary view does not necessarily store its result; a materialized view does.
Rewriting a subquery as a join can change duplicates, and does not guarantee faster execution.

notes.title: Set operations and type conversion in SQL

blocks.text: SELECT ID FROM A UNION SELECT ID FROM B; combines compatible result columns and removes duplicate rows by default.
UNION ALL retains duplicates.
Explicit UNION DISTINCT is accepted in some dialects, including PostgreSQL; it is not a separate algebra rule.
INTERSECT returns common rows; EXCEPT returns first-result rows absent from the second.
Inputs need the same column count and compatible corresponding types.
CAST('42' AS INTEGER) converts an expression to a requested type if the value permits it.
CONVERT is vendor-specific and can also perform type conversion; specify the SQL dialect when comparing it with CAST.
In SELECT xyz FROM table1 UNION xyz FROM table2, the second SELECT is missing.
In the corrected query, xyz is a selected column/expression, not a table name.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
PostgreSQL: Combining queries
PostgreSQL: Value expressions
Selection σ filters tuples; projection π retains attributes and removes duplicate tuples under set semantics.
Rename ρ changes relation or attribute names.
Union, difference and intersection require union-compatible schemas.
Difference R−S is not commutative; union and intersection are.
Inner joins are commutative up to attribute order when predicates are adjusted; left outer joins are not generally commutative.
Identify the join variant before predicting its behavior.
A Cartesian product has |R|×|S| tuples and degree degree(R)+degree(S), renaming conflicting attributes if necessary.
Join equals selection over a product; intersection can be derived from difference.
A common minimal basis contains selection, projection, union, difference, product and rename.
Assignment is a useful notation, not an indispensable primitive; lists of basic operations vary across textbooks.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module

notes.title: Relational calculus: state the desired facts

blocks.text: Relational algebra specifies a sequence of operations and is procedural at the logical level.
Relational calculus specifies a predicate describing desired results and is declarative/nonprocedural.
A tuple variable ranges over tuples; a domain variable ranges over individual attribute values.
Safe/range-restricted expressions produce results bounded by the database's active domain.
Tuple form {s | Student(s) AND s.Major='CS'} selects student tuples with that major.
A domain form can request names n satisfying ∃i,m (Student(i,n,m) AND m='CS').
Existential quantification means some matching tuple exists; universal quantification means every required case meets a condition.
SQL is declarative even though an optimizer later chooses a procedural execution plan.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module
A transaction groups operations into one logical unit.
Atomicity applies all its effects or none.
Consistency means a correct transaction preserves declared invariants.
Isolation controls interference between concurrent transactions; serializable isolation provides behavior equivalent to some serial execution.
Durability preserves committed effects after a crash, typically through durable logging rather than forcing every data page immediately.
For a transfer, subtracting 100 from one balance and adding 100 to another must commit together; losing either half violates atomicity and may violate the total-balance invariant.
BEGIN starts work, COMMIT completes it, ROLLBACK undoes uncommitted work and SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate rollback point.
A failed transaction may roll back while other users' committed transactions remain.
SQL transaction syntax and error-handling constructs differ by DBMS; @@ERROR/IF is SQL Server-specific.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module

notes.title: Choose a design technique from the requirement

blocks.text: Normalization reduces dependency-driven anomalies.
Indexing supplies search paths.
Denormalization deliberately repeats or precomputes facts to reduce selected read costs, increasing maintenance work.
Partitioning divides rows or columns; replication creates copies to improve locality or availability while complicating updates.
These techniques can coexist.
An e-commerce or gaming label alone does not select one.
Privacy requires a threat model.
Authentication verifies identity; role-based authorization limits allowed records/actions; encryption protects data at rest or in transit; auditing records activity.
Both encryption and access control can protect patient data.
Scalability, availability, fast retrieval, redundancy control and security are all reasonable design considerations.
Functional requirements describe behavior; nonfunctional requirements quantify qualities such as 99.9% uptime or response time.
Authentication and encryption mechanisms alone do not uniquely establish that distinction.
In a CMS, tags/categories describe meaning, while foreign keys preserve valid references between content and tags.
A ContentTag(ContentID,TagID) association models multiple tags per item; these functions complement each other.
Fundamental of Database Systems module
Advanced Database Systems module

notes.title: Integrated design: student registration and dormitory allocation

blocks.text: State the rules first: each student belongs to one department, may enroll in many courses, and has at most one current dorm assignment.
Each course accepts many students; each dorm holds at most six students.
Identify Department, Student, Course and Dorm entities; Enrollment is the M:N relationship with Grade.
Use Department(DeptID,Name), Student(SID,Name,DeptID,DormID), Course(CID,Title), Enrollment(SID,CID,Grade) and Dorm(DormID,FloorNumber).
Declare all entity IDs primary keys; Student.DeptID and Student.DormID reference their parents; Enrollment has composite key (SID,CID) and both references.
Make DormID nullable until assignment.
Separate StudentPhone(SID,Phone) for multiple contacts.
Normalize repeated department/course facts into their owning tables.
A simple foreign key does not enforce the six-student capacity; use a concurrency-safe trigger, allocation transaction or explicit slot design with six unique slots per dorm.
Worked example

items.text: Complete the reference as FOREIGN KEY (DormID) REFERENCES Dorm(DormID). STUDENT is the referencing child; DORM is referenced. Consistent names and an added Student.DormID column are required before execution.

blocks.text: Justify each answer using the schema, SQL rules and stated assumptions.
Owner and strong entity can both describe the entity supporting a weak entity; row and record are synonyms in a relational table; difference and set-difference are the same operator.
DELETE, UPDATE and the invalid command REMOVE are not DROP; a question asking which is not DROP can therefore admit several choices.
Compare all choices with the relevant rule before selecting an answer.
For invalid SQL, identify the syntax error and validate the corrected statement before analyzing its result.
For unsupported cardinalities, request business rules and direction.
For best/efficient/important questions, specify workload, quality goal or comparison baseline.
A diagram-dependent conclusion needs the missing diagram or an explicit description of its relevant symbols.
Identify the smallest clarification needed when a question does not support a unique answer.

notes.title: Algebra operator lists and derivable operations

blocks.text: A list of basic relational-algebra operators is a teaching convention, distinct from a claim that every listed operation is logically indispensable. The course module uses selection, projection, Cartesian product, set difference, union and intersection as its basic-operation list. Natural join and assignment are not members of that particular list.

Under set semantics, union includes tuples from either compatible input, intersection retains tuples common to both, and difference keeps first-input tuples absent from the second. Intersection can be expressed using difference, while a matching join can be expressed as selection over a Cartesian product. A smaller primitive basis may therefore omit intersection even when it is introduced as a basic operation.
Fundamental of Database Systems module · page 24

An object-relational DBMS retains relational data management while supporting richer extensions such as user-defined data types, functions and operators. PostgreSQL is an example. Richer relational types do not by themselves require all data to form a parent–child tree; that representation is the defining concern of hierarchical modeling.
